newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Airports report passenger, cargo traffic lift.
newsitem.headline: Airports report passenger, cargo traffic lift.

text.p: World airports on Friday reported a seven per cent rise in passenger traffic and five per cent in cargo in the first half of 1996, backing forecasts of strong growth for the airline industry to the end of the century.

Figures released by the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) also showed that U.S. hubs held the top four places in the global league for the busiest passenger and cargo airports between January and June.

ACI, whose report was based on returns from 458 member airports around the globe, said 1.2 billion travellers passed through them in the first half of the year -- 73 million more than in the January-June period last year.

Chicago's O'Hare was the world's busiest passenger airport, seeing 33.5 million people pass through, followed by Atlanta whose share during the first six months was boosted 16.2 per cent to 32.4 million due to the Olympic Games.

In third position was Los Angeles with 27.9 million passengers, followed by Dallas/Fort Worth with 27 million, London's Heathrow with 26,5 and Tokyo's Haneda, Japan's main domestic hub, with 21,9 million.
Cargo moved totalled 23.3 million tonnes, one million tonnes more than last year, while aircraft movements were up two per cent to 23.3 million.
ACI director-general Otis Dunham said the figures "lend support to recent airline forecasts of over seven per cent annual growth in passenger trafic through to the year 2000.
"This is very healthy growth, and all parties in the air transport industry must redouble their efforts to get more capacity out of the system."
This would imply "more efficient passenger and cargo processing, and the maximum use of new technologies both on the ground and in the air."
The largest percentage passenger growth this year, although from a low base, was recorded by ACI's Africa region which saw traffic climb by 7.7 per cent to a total of 12.9 million.

But North America, boosted by travel to the Olympic Games in Atlanta, saw growth of 7.1 per cent for a total of 608.8 million. Asia/Pacific airports saw 6.9 per cent more people passing through for a total of 168.7 million.

European region passengers were up 6.2 per cent to a total of 330.3 million, while in the Middle East they totalled 21.7 million, an increase of 5.9 per cent. Growth in Latin America and the Caribbean was only 1.7 per cent to 36.5 million.

In cargo, 12.5 million tonnes were moved by North American airports, an increase of 5.5 per cent over January-June 1995. But the biggest percentage rise -- 18.4 -- was returned by the Middle East for a total of 778,951 tonnes.
Asia/Pacific airport cargo moved grew four per cent to 4.4 million tonnes, while Europe saw a 3.8 per cent increase to 4.87 million.

Africa, which moves relatively little cargo by air, saw a 1.1 per cent drop to 189,544 tonnes, and Latin America and the Caribbean saw an even steeper decline of 9.8 per cent to a total of only 505,399 tonnes.

Top six cargo airports were Memphis, Tennessee, which moved 915,057 tonnes, Los Angeles with 821,149 tonnes, Miami with 815,585, New York's Kennedy with 779,544, Tokyo's Narita with 771,045 and Germany's Frankfurt with 722,451 tonnes moved.
